tagline: Hold a codebase to the standard it set for itself.
summary: An on-demand integrity audit that reads the repository's own constitution — declared invariants (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md), decision records, contracts and executable guards — then sweeps the code for drift across six universal classes: enforcement (authorization broader than declared, paths around the sole control point), deployment-value (silent tenant/region fallbacks that make a fresh deployment impersonate the first one), contract (schemas nothing loads, copies without drift tests), robustness (I/O without timeouts, silent-loss windows, unbounded reads), duplication and hygiene. Every candidate finding is counter-validated line by line in source and must cite the invariant it violates. In REMEDIATE mode it fixes at the root cause and ships a CI guard derived from the project's own sources of truth, so the drift class cannot recur; in REALIGN mode it judges a branch or diff against the core design before it lands.
capabilities: Derives the audit reference from the repo itself — invariants, ADRs, schemas, guard tests — and cites it in every finding; no invented principles
Sweeps six universal drift classes with concrete detection heuristics and grep recipes, adapted to the repo's language
Counter-validates every candidate in source before reporting; discarded candidates are counted as evidence of rigor
Severity set by the constitution, not the class: invariant-breaking authorization drift is critical, hygiene is minor
REMEDIATE fixes root causes only — one lot per severity theme, one commit per lot, the project's own gate green between lots
Every fixed class ships a derived guard (forbidden sets computed from the registry/config, drift tests against the source of truth) — integrity enforced, not documented
REALIGN mode audits only a diff: drift introduced and guards weakened (deleted/loosened tests, widened allowlists) before merge
Report-only by default; flags acceptance criteria that can only be validated live instead of faking them
